content.text:
I reviewed all seven open PRs against their current bases, the architecture docs, and the repo rules. I found one code blocker and one release gate blocker.

### Findings

1. **High — [#195](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/195) collapses distinct Cargo target dependencies.** The new [dependency iterator](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/blob/525b17ef47d7bec32cbc6da8161bada9a0587479/crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs#L393) reports only the first declaration for each `(kind, name)`, while the [rewrite](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/blob/525b17ef47d7bec32cbc6da8161bada9a0587479/crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo.rs#L480) changes every declaration with that key. A top-level dependency and a target dependency can use the same local name but refer to different packages or have different version constraints. Bumping one can then rewrite the other’s pin; the graph can also miss the other package entirely. Workspace inheritance is tracked by the same coarse key, so one inherited target declaration can cause a direct declaration to be treated as inherited. Keep target declarations distinct through graph construction and rewriting, and test differing aliases, constraints, and inheritance.

2. **High — [#188](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/188) has no CI checks and GitHub reports it as `UNSTABLE`.** This is the generated PR whose merge publishes version `0.10.1`. The repo’s [CI workflow](/Users/gabe/Projects/callisto/.github/workflows/callisto-ci.yml:4) covers PRs to `main`, but no check run is attached to this PR. Run the required validation on its exact head before merging.

3. **Low — [#192](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/192) rejects a valid platform-only group through its new constructor.** [The constructor](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/blob/46d58c9/crates/callisto-graph/src/config/groups.rs) validates only `package_members()`, making a group containing a platform manifest appear empty. The config resolution path accepts that member shape. Validate all members while checking package ownership separately.

### PR assessment

| PR | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| [#196](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/196) | Apply refactor follows the prior write order and retains the guarded version writes. No separate defect found; it is stacked on #195. |
| [#195](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/195) | **Request changes** for the Cargo target dependency issue. Its new black-box tests cover matching declarations, not differing ones. |
| [#193](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/193) | No issue found. Permit construction now uses the parsed dry-run flag; stacked on #190. |
| [#192](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/192) | Fix the platform-only constructor case before treating the new API as equivalent to config loading. |
| [#191](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/191) | No issue found. The retry retains final verification and has success and failure coverage. |
| [#190](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/190) | No issue found. The shared scanner preserves the prior helpers’ behavior. |
| [#188](https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/pull/188) | **Hold merge** until its exact release commit has passing checks. |

The completed checks for #190–#193 and #191 passed when queried; the macOS tests for #195 and #196 were still running. This was a diff and execution-path review; I did not run local Cargo tests against the PR heads or post review comments.
